profile.campus: Gallatin, Sumner County, Tennessee (Meta's Gallatin data center campus)
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 2 of 3 mapped in the newer cluster) is part of Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County, Tennessee, northeast of Nashville. Facebook announced the project in August 2020 after a three-year site-selection effort involving the Gallatin Economic Development Agency, the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development, and the Tennessee Valley Authority; the initial building was reported at 982,000 square feet with an $800 million investment, citing the area's infrastructure, workforce, and community partnership. Meta's own announcement confirms the Gallatin data center went live on November 14, 2024, with total Tennessee investment since grown to more than $1.5 billion, more than 1,100 peak skilled-trade construction workers, and now more than 100 operational jobs. TVA initially committed to bringing 220 megawatts of new solar generation to support the project; Meta's current fact sheet describes a Meta-supported total of 530 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity added in Tennessee as the campus has grown, alongside the facility's standard commitments to 100% renewable electricity, LEED Gold certification, and roughly 80% less water use than an average data center. Meta reports more than $1.4 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, including a $250,000 grant to the Gallatin Shalom Zone for restoration of a historic gymnasium, 30 acres of native pollinator habitat planted on-site, and a partnership with the Tennessee Environmental Council to install roughly 6,000 square feet of pollinator gardens across Sumner County middle schools. Meta does not publish a specific street address, current building count, or per-building square footage for individual Gallatin structures beyond the original 982,000-square-foot building reported at announcement; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

reading.body:
Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County, Tennessee went live in November 2024 after a multi-year recruitment process led by the Tennessee Valley Authority and the state economic development agency. The original building announced in 2020 was reported at 982,000 square feet with an $800 million investment; Meta now operates three mapped structures at the site as part of a campus that has grown to encompass $1.5 billion in total investment. Current per-building square footage and megawatt figures for the expanded campus are not published by Meta.

Meta has committed 530 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity across Tennessee to support the Gallatin campus as it has grown, against TVA's initial 220-megawatt solar commitment when the project was announced. Assuming 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, and applying the 530-megawatt figure as a conservative upper bound for IT load across the full campus, this translates roughly to 13,000 racks. The campus operates at LEED Gold certification, targets 100 percent renewable electricity, and uses roughly 80 percent less water than an average data center.

Gallatin ranks fifth among the four Tennessee facilities with published megawatt figures on this site, though most of Tennessee's 24 mapped data center facilities publish no capacity data. The campus sits in the Nashville metro area's growing advanced-manufacturing and data-center corridor, northeast of the city, in a region that has attracted large-scale investment alongside Meta's development. Tennessee's published capacity across all sources totals 12.13 megawatts, which does not account for Gallatin or most other mapped facilities in the state.
